headline: Islanders’ Calum Ritchie, Matias Maccelli leave game with injuries
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Islanders forwards Calum Ritchie and Matias Maccelli both left New York's 4-1 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs with injuries. No details on the severity were given.

The numbers say the loss of Maccelli would sting more. So far this season, the Islanders take 55.93% of the 5-on-5 expected goals when he plays, and the team's share is 7.31 points better with him than without. He has 6 points in 8 games and 0.89 goals above expected, so some of that output may cool, but his on-ice impact looks real. Ritchie is the opposite case: the Islanders' 5-on-5 share is 8.69 points worse with him (43.56% for him), and he is averaging 12.18 minutes with 2 points in 8 games. Losing him would change little on the ice. The bigger concern is the team itself. New York sits at 4-3-1, but its overall expected goals share is 44.2%, and it has been bailed out by goaltending, 11 goals saved above expected. That cushion rarely lasts, so any further thinning of the forward group makes it harder to keep winning games it is being outplayed in.
